chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Suleiman ibn Abu Zaynab, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
My father was saying: 'If there was a road for me to my house from Mina, I would not enter Makkah.'

key_terms.أَبِي: My father, referring to Imam al-Baqir (AS) in the narration of Imam al-Sadiq (AS)
key_terms.مَكَّةَ: Makkah, the holy city and site of the Kaaba
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, the sacred site near Makkah where pilgrims stay during Hajj

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Baqir (AS) prefer not to enter Makkah from Mina during Hajj?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates that his father, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him), used to say that if there were a direct path to his house from Mina, he would not enter the city of Makkah. This highlights the practice of avoiding unnecessary entry into the city during Hajj to minimize time spent outside the sacred precincts of Mina, Arafat, and Muzdalifah, or to avoid the crowds and potential distractions of the city. In Shia scholarly tradition, this reflects the principle of *ikhtiyar* (preference) for remaining in the primary stations of Hajj rather than engaging in optional visits, emphasizing spiritual focus and adherence to the Prophet's Sunnah of brevity in Makkah during the days of Tashriq.

en.sarwar: 9. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Mansur ibn al-‘Abbas from Ali ibn Asbat from Sulayman ibn abu Zaynabah from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
My father, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would say, “Had there been a road to my home from Mina’ I would not enter Makkah.’””
